clue.text: Brie melted in air? That's serious

indicators.note: the shuffled cheese is placed in the middle of the tune word

parts.note: an air is a tune or song

indicators.note: melted cheese loses its shape, so its letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether melted Brie is floating in the air, and is told the matter is grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'air' looks like the atmosphere but means a tune; 'melted' rearranges the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sobering makes a person grave and thoughtful, so it is a thing that is serious in effect.

clue.text: Charges about having lost good rifle

indicators.note: about means the remaining letters are turned around into a new order
having lost says a letter goes from the word before shuffling

explanation.surface: Accusations concerning a gun that went missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' takes G from CHARGES; 'about' shuffles CHARES.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through something is to search it hastily, a verb sense.

clue.text: Called out plot to capture animal shelter

indicators.note: to capture means the plot word holds the shelter word inside

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot
Noah's ark sheltered the animals

explanation.surface: Shouting about a scheme to seize a pet refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: To bark is to shout sharply, as in barking orders.

clue.text: Note on black French artist

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
noir is French for black

explanation.surface: A memo about a dark French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Renoir was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: English not crazy for flashy displays

indicators.note: crazy means wild or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The English are not mad about showy displays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' signals an anagram of ENGLISH NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon lights are bright glowing advertising signs, flashy by design.

clue.text: Papers returned with date inserted in agreement

indicators.note: the date letter is put inside the backwards papers word
returned means the word for papers is read backwards

parts.note: the media are newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Documents sent back with a date added to a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns MEDIA into AIDEM; D goes in after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad idem is Latin legal phrasing for 'to the same thing', describing parties whose minds meet.

clue.text: Outstanding former PM is straight up

parts.note: an outstanding bill is due, not yet paid
Lord North was British Prime Minister 1770-1782

explanation.surface: An exceptional past prime minister is completely honest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' means owed, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: On a map north is at the top, so due north is directly up the page.

clue.text: Quickly pass on insult

explanation.surface: Hurriedly forwarding an offensive remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Pass on is a euphemism for die, and the exclamation is a curt rude retort.

clue.text: Bring down average speed

parts.note: the mode is one kind of statistical average
rate means speed

explanation.surface: Lowering the mean velocity, as a traffic engineer might.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate is to lessen or tone down, reducing intensity.

clue.text: Drama not composed willy-nilly

indicators.note: composed in the sense of put together afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A play that was never written properly, cobbled together any old how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' signals an anagram of DRAMA NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Willy-nilly means haphazardly, without plan or choice, which is the sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Outside link accommodating short study

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the link word holds the other piece

parts.note: a bond is a tie or link

indicators.note: short means the study word loses its final letter

parts.note: to eye something is to study it

explanation.surface: An external connection housing a brief piece of research.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts EYE to EY, which BOND is 'accommodating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beyond as a preposition means outside the limits or reach of something.

clue.text: Apparently true conservative Republican can be taken in

parts.note: food that can be taken in, eaten, is edible

explanation.surface: A believable right-wing politician can still fool people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be taken in' reads as 'can be fooled' but means 'can be eaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: Credible means believable, plausible on its face, so seemingly true.

clue.text: Think about returning wine present

indicators.note: returning means the wine word and the present word are read backwards together

parts.note: red is wine
now is the present time

explanation.surface: Giving back a bottle of wine as a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns REDNOW round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: To wonder about something is to ponder or consider it.

clue.text: City replaces masthead in general correspondence

indicators.note: replaces says the city takes the place of the head of the mast in the other word

parts.note: common means general, widespread
the head, first letter, of mast is M
Paris is a capital city

explanation.surface: A city newspaper swaps its title banner in its general letters page.
explanation.walkthrough: The second M of COMMON gives way to PARIS. 'correspondence' looks like letters, but it means likeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence as similarity or matching corresponds to a comparison between things.

clue.text: Encourage cook, perhaps, to provide snack

parts.note: to egg on is to encourage or urge
toasting is one way to cook, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Urging a chef to rustle up a light bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg on toast is a quick light meal, a typical snack.

clue.text: Record second thoughts about recent requirement for country reps

parts.note: CD, compact disc, is a record

indicators.note: about means the second-thoughts letters go round the recent word

parts.note: PS, postscript, adds afterthoughts to a letter
late can mean recent, as in the late news

explanation.surface: Logging afterthoughts on something new needed by national representatives.
explanation.walkthrough: In the answer CD means Corps Diplomatique.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomats' cars carry CD number plates, so a country's envoys need them.

clue.text: Philosopher irritated when declared to be like everyone else

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, so the words are taken as heard

parts.note: David Hume was a Scottish philosopher; irritated means annoyed

explanation.surface: A thinker gets cross on being called ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanoid means having human form, so resembling all the rest of us people.

clue.text: Whole green bananas can cause a bad reaction

parts.note: all means the whole

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Eating whole unripe bananas may upset you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit; it signals an anagram of GREEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergen is a substance that triggers an allergic response in the body.

clue.text: It requires perfect vision to get this score on board

definitions.text: It requires perfect vision to get this score on board

parts.words: It requires perfect vision to get this score on board
parts.note: in darts the double ring at the top of the board is worth double twenty, and twenty-twenty is the term for good eyesight

explanation.surface: A darts player needs sharp eyes to hit a high score.
explanation.walkthrough: Double top in darts is double twenty; 'perfect vision' is 20/20 vision, so a double twenty twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: Double top is the darts name for the double-twenty segment, the score a player hits there.

clue.text: Food for new recruits

definitions.meaning: a batch of people newly taken on

explanation.surface: Provisions laid on for a fresh batch of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Intake covers both what is eaten and the people admitted at one time.

clue.text: Get to chaps minding tot

indicators.note: minding as looking after, so the chaps word keeps the other inside

parts.note: men are chaps
to tot up is to add

explanation.surface: Getting some lads to look after a toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' is a child in the surface but means add up.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to someone is to annoy them, which is what madden means.

clue.text: Deplore being endlessly cruel

definitions.meaning: to deplore is to feel deep grief over, to lament
cruel without its ends is rue, and to rue is to be sorry for, so this half leads to the answer through a synonym

explanation.surface: Condemning someone for constant cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims cruel to RUE, which is not the answer but a synonym of it: the second half defines by way of a mini-clue, an unusual and much-criticised device.
explanation.definitionFit: Deplore in its older sense of lament matches feeling sorrow or remorse over something.

clue.text: Two flats? That sounds rich

indicators.note: this phrase says the two words for flat, spoken, give the answer

parts.note: flat can mean low (as a level) and dead (as a flat battery or drink)

explanation.surface: Owning two apartments certainly seems wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flats' looks like apartments; it is two synonyms of flat, LOW and DEAD, said together.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is slang for very wealthy, having plenty of money.

clue.text: With constant coverage, novel can't get contract

indicators.note: with, read together with the later word coverage, says the constant word holds the shuffled piece
with coverage says the constant word covers, wraps round, the shuffled piece

parts.note: true can mean constant or loyal

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A steady stream of publicity, yet a book still fails to land a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' turns CANT into NCAT, which TRUE covers.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate is to shorten by cutting, a sense of contract as reduce in size.

clue.text: Extremely ticklish open garments made of leather?

indicators.note: extremely means each word gives up its extreme letters, the first and last

explanation.surface: Skimpy underwear that tickles, perhaps fashioned from leather.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of 'ticklish', 'open' and 'garments' give TH, ON and GS. The wordplay also describes the skimpy garments, so the clue reads almost as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong was originally a strip or strap of leather, so thongs are leather things, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Independent small spacecraft, one based in Sicily?

parts.note: a lander is a spacecraft built to set down on a planet or moon

explanation.surface: A free-standing little probe touching down in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is an island, so someone living there is an islander; the question mark marks it as one example.

clue.text: Second-hand vehicles lacking leads had to be carried

indicators.note: lacking leads means each word loses its leading letter

parts.note: used means second-hand
vans are vehicles

explanation.surface: Used cars without their front ends had to be hauled away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-hand vehicles' reads as the definition, but it is the wordplay: USED VANS without U and V.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedans were sedan chairs, enclosed seats borne on poles by carriers.

clue.text: Place trap underground with modern technology

parts.note: to inter is to place in the ground, as the clue's 'underground' spells out
a net is a trap

explanation.surface: Laying a snare below ground with up-to-date gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase meaning 'place underground' is split, with the trap word sitting between its two halves in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The internet is the global computer network, a defining recent technology.
